title: Changes deserve their own artifacts.
lede: A release records a model state. A change artifact records the difference.

takeaway: Publish the change. Query it from tools that support the profile.
notes: A model release is an identified state; a change is also publishable structured data. Compare two source/target releases pinned by manifest digest. The proposed change profile records persistent model/entity references, property or relationship addresses, operations, typed before/after values, units when relevant, and explicit missing/null/deletion semantics. The example values are illustrative and make no engineering or approval claim.

ifc-git is one possible semantic comparison producer. Its proposed direction is whole-file ingestion producing delta layers with recorded identity matching. Another engine may produce the common contract. A human-readable text report is a view of the structured change, not the canonical query interface. A composable native layer and a typed query representation must share declared comparison scope and identities; a profile must define their consistency rules.

OCI stores and distributes artifacts; clients or a rebuildable indexing service query their content. A typed change table could use Parquet, but this encoding is a proposal rather than a finalized standard. Publishing ordinary whole-file releases works without any comparison engine. Branching and merging are optional application workflows, not prerequisites for exchange.
